findings: findJpegMarker returns true for SOI-prefixed bytes even when EOI missing; truncation sets an error but does not change isJpeg=false. This contradicts header note that truncated JPEG returns false. processImageFile only rejects a null decoded image, not the recorded truncation itself; native decoder acceptance untested.

jpegPayload hashes bytes from the first SOS marker to end, excluding prior headers/tables as well as EXIF. Therefore the normalized checksum cannot be treated as byte-file identity. No decoder equivalence or safety conclusion; JPEG parser bounds not dynamically probed and deferred ASAN not run.

processImageFile reads compressed data once, computes normalized digest from that buffer and passes decoded QImage to processImage. With algos0 it can create ok Media without successful full decode. This is a checksum-only path, not a complete format validation.

Video decoder is opened before processVideo separately opens file for fullMd5; no source identity/stamp verification between checksum and frame indexing visible. Video processing sets oktrue after makeVideoIndex even if indexer capped/encountered errors; decoder-level error policy remains unread.

readDirectory enumerates current-level entries then recursively descends each collected directory before moving to the next sibling. README breadth-first duplicate-inode selection description is not a general match for this traversal. Default minFileSize1024 excludes smaller loose image/video files; archive member handling has different gates.

followSymlinks defaults false; POSIX dupInodesfalse enables visited FileId suppression, Windows dupInodestrue disables it by default. Enabling link following while permitting duplicate inodes lacks a separate directory-cycle guard here. No recursive link fixture executed.

resolveLinks containment uses startsWith(_topDirPath) without a path-separator boundary. Existing/freshness checks use earlier QFileInfo entry even when effective path changes. Runtime canonical/FileId behavior not qualified.

scanDirectory appends parsed include/exclude regexes without clearing existing vectors, so reusing a Scanner with changed params can retain old patterns. readArchive does not call includePath for individual member paths; current expected filtering and archive queues can differ. No Qt scanner run.

Missing directory/archive open failures return from that subtree while expected entries may remain; scanDirectory can still emit completed/no changes. Engine removal handling is unread, so no claim of actual database loss.

flush clears waiting queues but not _queuedWork; active cancellation cleanup skips context/thread accounting branches. Scheduler and error map lifetime need reuse/concurrency runtime checks. Source-only findings, no background process started.
